title: Begging out of the NBC contract
summary: Budd asks to be released from his union contract because he wants to play, against his wife's wishes.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I don't have the slightest idea who he was because I didn't know any of these guys up there at that time. But any way, you know, I did learn a lot about writing for the Hammond organ from this thing. This really gave me courage. So any way I finally begged off, I said, man, look, this is really too confining for me, I mean I can't get them other things, I certainly wish you would let me go out of this contract. Now I had a written contract, I had a union contract. I mean, a lot of guys was ghost writing, and I was really at (Inaudible) NBC. I had this contract.

So the guy said well man we're more than satisfied with your work, man, please don't leave. We all appreciate you, the cat, the librarian and everybody is begging me to stay. And I told my wife, I said, I'm going to leave and she thought I was absolutely insane because like I was making a lot of money --

I wanted to play. I was making a lot of money up there and I probably could have been really great now because if I'd stayed I would have been studying more and everything, you know, trying to keep up.
Let me say, Budd, you couldn't be any greater than you are right now, no way if you'd done anything, because you are really great.
Let's hang this for just a second.
